uncited: Coarse-to-Fine Hierarchical Sampling is a strategy that improves the learning of high-frequency details in Neural Radiance Fields by performing two tiers of volume sampling [Coarse-to-Fine NeRF](3406-coarse-to-fine-nerf.md).

It solves the problem of inefficient uniform sampling, where most samples fall in empty space, by using a coarse network to identify opaque regions and then clustering a second set of samples near those regions to train a fine network [Coarse-to-Fine NeRF](3406-coarse-to-fine-nerf.md).

It sets itself apart from standard uniform sampling by adaptively concentrating computational effort on visible geometry, and from its sibling [TermiNeRF](8828-terminerf.md) by not explicitly modeling termination probabilities but rather relying on opacity-based importance sampling [Coarse-to-Fine NeRF](3406-coarse-to-fine-nerf.md).
